ev.k2_sweet_pot.title: The pot on the top shelf
ev.k2_sweet_pot.text: On the shelf right under the roof sits a sealed pot of something sweet, saved for the feast. If you drag over a basket and put an upturned bowl on top, you can just reach it. Nobody is home.
ev.k2_sweet_pot.climb.success: You licked your fingers, put the lid back and spent the rest of the day as the best-behaved child in the world. Nobody found out - well, almost nobody.
ev.k2_sweet_pot.climb.failure: The basket slid, the bowl followed, and the pot came down after both of them. The sweets ran all over the floor, the feast was a plain one that year, and you got a hiding on top of it.
ev.k2_sweet_pot.ask: Ask for just a tiny taste
ev.k2_sweet_pot.ask.success: The grown-ups exchanged a look and let you lick the lid. It was better than the whole pot.
ev.k2_sweet_pot.ask.failure: 'It's for the feast,' they said. You counted the days on your fingers and ran out of fingers.
ev.k2_sweet_pot.wait.ok: Every day you went to the shelf and just looked. At the feast you got the biggest piece - for patience.
ev.k2_haircut.title: The little barber
ev.k2_haircut.text: You found the sharp knife the grown-ups use to cut thread, and decided that your hair keeps getting in your eyes and must go. There is no one around.
ev.k2_haircut.cut.success: It came out surprisingly even. The grown-ups gasped for a long time, and then someone said, 'You know, that's not bad!'
ev.k2_haircut.cut.failure: There was a bald patch in front and a tuft sticking out at the side like a clump of dry grass. The neighbours' children laughed until it grew back.
ev.k2_haircut.dog: Better give the dog a haircut
ev.k2_haircut.dog.success: The dog put up with it as long as it could, then walked off with half its coat and the air of someone deeply insulted. You laughed until you got hiccups.
ev.k2_haircut.dog.failure: The dog did not put up with it. You got off with a fright and a scratch, and the knife was taken away from you for good.
ev.k2_haircut.put_back.ok: You put the knife back where you found it and even straightened it so it lay just so. Your hair still got in your eyes, but your conscience was clear.
ev.k2_hide_basket.title: In the basket
ev.k2_hide_basket.text: You climbed into the big basket in the corner so that everyone would have to look for you. At first they called cheerfully, then anxiously, and now someone has already run to the neighbours.
ev.k2_hide_basket.come_out: Climb out and shout, 'Here I am!'
ev.k2_hide_basket.come_out.ok: You were grabbed, hugged, smacked and hugged again, all at once. Afterwards the basket was put where you couldn't climb into it.
ev.k2_hide_basket.stay.success: They found you by your sneeze. The grown-ups hugged you so hard your bones creaked, and only then did they scold you.
ev.k2_hide_basket.stay.failure: You fell asleep in the basket while the whole street searched ditches and back yards until dark. When they found you, nobody laughed - and that was worse than any thrashing.
ev.k2_watering.title: The little helper
ev.k2_watering.text: In the morning the grown-ups filled a big jar with water and went off to work. You decided to help, and watered everything in the yard: the vegetable patch, the tree, the dog and the hearth. The jar is empty, the hearth is hissing, the dog is wet.
ev.k2_watering.fetch.success: You brought back a little jug, spilling half of it on the way. The grown-ups didn't know whether to laugh or be proud, so they did both.
ev.k2_watering.fetch.failure: You slipped at the water's edge, the jug broke, and you came home soaked to the ears. At least nobody doubts that you tried.
ev.k2_watering.hide.ok: They found you by your wet footprints. The grown-ups spent a long time asking who had flooded the hearth, though the footprints were small and led straight to you.
ev.k2_watering.tell: Meet the grown-ups and tell them everything
ev.k2_watering.tell.ok: You told them honestly, even about the dog. The grown-ups sighed and went for more water, and took you with them to carry the smallest jug.
ev.k2_dark.title: The dark
ev.k2_dark.text: You woke in the night. The fire has burned down, the house is pitch black, and something is rustling in the corner. A mouse, maybe. Or maybe not.
ev.k2_dark.wake.ok: Someone sleepily pulled you close, said it was a mouse, and fell asleep before you could ask if they were sure.
ev.k2_dark.look.success: You crept to the corner, and a mouse shot out from under a basket, more frightened than you were. In the morning you told everyone how you had chased off a monster.
ev.k2_dark.look.failure: You tripped over a pot, it clattered, you screamed, and the whole house woke up, and the neighbours too. The rustling remained a mystery.
ev.k2_dark.cover: Pull the cover over your head and hold your breath
ev.k2_dark.cover.ok: You lay like that until dawn, listening to every sound. In the morning there was nothing in the corner but old rags, and you yawned all day.
ev.k2_dark_later.title: A rustle in the dark
ev.k2_dark_later.text: Something is rustling in the yard tonight - just like that time in childhood when you went into the dark corner to face the monster. Only now there is nobody to check but you.
ev.k2_dark_later.go: Take a light and go out
ev.k2_dark_later.go.success: Behind the woodpile, curled up in a ball, sat a lost little child from the next street, cold and tear-stained. You took the child home, and the family bowed to you every time you met for a long while after.
ev.k2_dark_later.go.failure: It was only the wind in the dry leaves. But you stumbled in the dark and burned your hand on your own light.
ev.k2_dark_later.neighbors.ok: The neighbours came with sticks, searched the yard and found nobody. They went home grumbling, and one of them said you were braver as a child, by all accounts.
ev.k2_scary_neighbor.title: The frightening neighbour
ev.k2_scary_neighbor.text: Two houses down lives an old man with a pitted face and one eye. The older children say he eats naughty ones. Today he is sitting on his doorstep, beckoning to you with a finger and hiding something in his fist.
ev.k2_scary_neighbor.approach.success: In his fist was a little bird carved from wood. The old man showed you how it nodded its head, and laughed - for the first time in years, it seemed. Since then you run to see him every day.
ev.k2_scary_neighbor.approach.failure: You got within three steps, and then the old man began to cough - a terrible, whistling cough. You fled without looking back, and the wooden bird he had carved for you stayed in his hand.
ev.k2_scary_neighbor.run.ok: You ran all the way home, and for a long time afterwards you took the long way round his house.
ev.k2_scary_neighbor.stone: Throw a pebble at him, like the big children do
ev.k2_scary_neighbor.stone.ok: The pebble fell far short. He only looked at you with his one eye - and that look made you ashamed for many days.
ev.k2_neighbor_legacy.title: The old man's gift
ev.k2_neighbor_legacy.text: The one-eyed old man you used to visit as a little child has died. Before he died, he asked for his carving knives and an unfinished wooden bird to be given to you.
ev.k2_neighbor_legacy.learn: Finish the bird and learn to carve
ev.k2_neighbor_legacy.learn.ok: The bird came out a little crooked, but it nodded its head, just like the first one. You have kept the knives with you ever since.
ev.k2_neighbor_legacy.keep: Keep it all as a keepsake
ev.k2_neighbor_legacy.keep.ok: You wrapped the knives in a clean cloth and put them away with the bird. Sometimes you take them out and remember his laugh.
ev.k2_neighbor_legacy.sell.ok: A craftsman at the market paid a fair price and turned them over in his hands for a long time: 'Old work. Nobody makes them like this now.' You kept the bird.
ev.k2_mask.title: The mask
ev.k2_mask.text: At the festival a man in a huge mask burst out of the crowd - fangs, bulging eyes and a beard of shaggy grass. He bent right down to you and growled.
ev.k2_mask.hide: Burst into tears and hide behind the grown-ups
ev.k2_mask.hide.ok: You clung to someone's clothes and didn't let go until the festival was over. The mask came back in your dreams twice more.
ev.k2_mask.touch.success: The fang was wooden and warm. The mask laughed in a human voice, and the dancer gave you a ribbon from his costume.
ev.k2_mask.touch.failure: The mask snapped its jaws, and you sat down hard in the dust. You dreamed of fangs for a week.
ev.k2_mask.growl.success: The mask jumped back as if frightened, and everyone around roared with laughter. 'What a beast!' someone said, and the name stuck for a long time.
ev.k2_mask.growl.failure: Your growl came out as a squeak. The mask shook its head and went off to scare someone more worthwhile.
ev.k2_big_dog.title: The dog on the path
ev.k2_big_dog.text: A huge strange dog is lying in the middle of the path home. It isn't growling, but it isn't moving either - just watching you with yellow eyes. The only way round is through the thorns.
ev.k2_big_dog.pass: Walk past without looking at it
ev.k2_big_dog.pass.success: You walked past, counting your steps and not breathing. The dog yawned after you. Only at home did you notice that you had been clenching your fists the whole time.
ev.k2_big_dog.pass.failure: The dog jumped up and barked once - just because. You ran, fell, skinned your knee and got home in tears.
ev.k2_big_dog.around.ok: The thorns scratched your legs and tore your clothes, but the dog was left behind. It didn't seem to notice your heroic feat at all.
ev.k2_big_dog.share: Give it your piece of food
ev.k2_big_dog.share.success: The dog took the treat gently, sniffed your palm and walked you all the way to the gate. Now it waits for you on the path every day.
ev.k2_big_dog.share.failure: The dog swallowed it without chewing and looked to see if there was more. There wasn't. You had to go through the thorns after all.
ev.k2_lost_field.title: Lost
ev.k2_lost_field.text: You chased a dragonfly into the tall growth, and when it flew away there was nothing around you but stalks taller than your head. You can't see home, and you can't hear anyone.
ev.k2_lost_field.shout: Stay where you are and shout
ev.k2_lost_field.shout.success: You shouted until you were hoarse. They found you by your voice and carried you out, and you fell asleep before supper.
ev.k2_lost_field.shout.failure: The wind in the stalks was louder than you. They found you only at dusk, with torches, and you were bitten all over by midges.
ev.k2_lost_field.smoke.success: You sniffed the air like a dog, went where it smelled of the hearth, and came out right by your own yard. Nobody at home had even had time to be frightened.
ev.k2_lost_field.smoke.failure: The smoke was someone else's - a herders' fire. The herders fed you and brought you home by evening, where everyone was beside themselves.
ev.k2_lost_field.sit.ok: You cried until you fell asleep among the stalks. You woke up in someone's arms on the way home, and for a long time you didn't know where you were.
ev.k2_tall_tale.title: The monster behind the wall
ev.k2_tall_tale.text: You told the neighbours' children that a monster with three tails lives behind the old wall. You made it up on the spot, but they believed you - and now even the grown-ups are asking what exactly you saw.
ev.k2_tall_tale.confess.ok: The grown-ups laughed, the children sulked. But one old man said, 'A good monster. Pity it's made up' - and you felt less ashamed.
ev.k2_tall_tale.embellish.success: You told them about the scales, the eyes like coals, and how the monster steals other children's toys. The grown-ups roared, the children didn't sleep all night, and you became the street's chief storyteller.
ev.k2_tall_tale.embellish.failure: Someone asked what colour the third tail was, and you got muddled. For a week the neighbours' children called you a fibber.
ev.k2_tall_tale.swear.ok: You swore so fiercely that they believed you - and forbade all the children to go near the wall. Now you can't go there either.
ev.k2_storyteller_grown.title: The storyteller
ev.k2_storyteller_grown.text: One evening by the fire someone remembers how, as a toddler, you invented a monster with three tails. 'Tell us something,' the neighbours ask, and even the old folk shuffle closer.
ev.k2_storyteller_grown.tell.success: The fire burned down to embers and nobody left. By morning your story was being retold at the other end of the street - with additions.
ev.k2_storyteller_grown.tell.failure: You started off briskly, but halfway through you forgot where you were going with it. Your listeners yawned politely.
ev.k2_storyteller_grown.joke.ok: 'The monster grew up and moved away,' you said, and everyone laughed. Sometimes that's enough.
ev.k2_imaginary_friend.title: The invisible friend
ev.k2_imaginary_friend.text: You have a friend nobody else can see. You call him Rustle, he lives in the corner behind the hearth, and at meals you leave a bit of food for him. The grown-ups are starting to exchange worried looks.
ev.k2_imaginary_friend.defend.ok: 'He'll be hurt,' you said so seriously that nobody argued any more. The grown-ups decided it would pass on its own, and started leaving crumbs in the corner.
ev.k2_imaginary_friend.goodbye: Say that Rustle has gone away
ev.k2_imaginary_friend.goodbye.ok: The grown-ups sighed with relief. But for a long time you kept peeking behind the hearth in secret, in case he had come back.
ev.k2_imaginary_friend.healer: Let the grown-ups call a healer
ev.k2_imaginary_friend.healer.christian: Let the grown-ups take you to the priest
ev.k2_imaginary_friend.healer.islamic: Let the mullah say a prayer over you
ev.k2_imaginary_friend.healer.jewish: Let the grown-ups take you to the rabbi
ev.k2_imaginary_friend.healer.dharmic: Let the grown-ups take you to a holy man at the temple
ev.k2_imaginary_friend.healer.east_asian: Let a diviner drive the strange spirit away
ev.k2_imaginary_friend.healer.polytheist: Let a priest see what spirit has settled in the house
ev.k2_imaginary_friend.healer.mesoameric: Let a priest smoke you with copal
ev.k2_imaginary_friend.healer.andean: Let a healer read the coca leaves
ev.k2_imaginary_friend.healer.african: Let a diviner ask the ancestors
ev.k2_imaginary_friend.healer.success: You were studied for a long time, and then the grown-ups were told, 'Leave it. A friend like that comes to kind children and leaves by himself when they grow up.'
ev.k2_imaginary_friend.healer.failure: There was a great deal of chanting, smoke and sprinkling of water over you. Rustle vanished after that - or perhaps he just took offence.
ev.k2_imaginary_return.title: An old friend
ev.k2_imaginary_return.text: In a hard year, with no one to say a word to, you suddenly catch yourself talking out loud to Rustle - your invisible friend from childhood. And, strangely enough, it helps.
ev.k2_imaginary_return.talk: Talk to him a little longer
ev.k2_imaginary_return.talk.ok: You told him everything that had piled up. As always, he didn't interrupt.
ev.k2_imaginary_return.people: Laugh at yourself and go and see people
ev.k2_imaginary_return.people.success: You dropped in on the neighbours for no reason at all. They sat you down, fed you and listened - it turned out they had had a hard year too.
ev.k2_imaginary_return.people.failure: The neighbours had no time for you. You went home and finished your talk with Rustle after all.
ev.k2_big_kids_secret.title: The oath
ev.k2_big_kids_secret.text: For the first time the big children of the street took you along - to their secret place in the ruins of an old house. Their treasures are hidden there: potsherds, feathers, a seashell. Before you left, they made you swear to keep quiet. And now, in the evening, the grown-ups want to know where you were half the day.
ev.k2_big_kids_secret.keep.ok: They asked nicely and not so nicely, and you only shook your head. The next day the big children already knew you hadn't told, and let you hold the shell.
ev.k2_big_kids_secret.tell.ok: The grown-ups forbade the children to go into the ruins. The big ones worked out who had blabbed, and never took you along again.
ev.k2_big_kids_secret.lie: Say you were playing at the neighbours'
ev.k2_big_kids_secret.lie.success: They believed you. For the first time you found out how heavy a secret is to carry - and how nice.
ev.k2_big_kids_secret.lie.failure: The neighbours had just come by to ask whether their children were at your house. The lie was short; the conversation was long.
ev.k2_oath_repaid.title: An old oath
ev.k2_oath_repaid.text: One of those big children who once took you into the ruins has long since grown up and become someone of standing. He recognises you in the street: 'You're that little one who never gave us away!'
ev.k2_oath_repaid.help: Ask for help with your affairs
ev.k2_oath_repaid.help.ok: He introduced you to the right people and lent you a little himself, with no interest. 'For the seashell,' he said with a wink.
ev.k2_oath_repaid.remember.ok: You sat until dark, going over everything that was in that pile of treasures. It turns out he still keeps the shell.
ev.k2_bedtime_story.title: One more story
ev.k2_bedtime_story.text: Every evening you demand the same story - about the clever tortoise and the stupid giant - and woe betide anyone who skips a single word. Tonight the storyteller has fallen asleep right in the middle.
ev.k2_bedtime_story.wake: Shake them awake and demand the ending
ev.k2_bedtime_story.wake.success: Without opening their eyes, the storyteller finished the tale - but quite differently: this time the tortoise flew off to the moon. You decided that was even better.
ev.k2_bedtime_story.wake.failure: The storyteller only snored and rolled over. You lay in the dark, cross with the whole world.
ev.k2_bedtime_story.finish.ok: You finished it in a whisper, and in your version the tortoise outwitted the giant twice. The storyteller, it turned out, wasn't asleep, and later passed your ending on to others.
ev.k2_bedtime_story.sleep.ok: You fell asleep snuggled against the storyteller's side, and in your dream the tortoise won after all.
ev.k2_tale_passed.title: That same story
ev.k2_tale_passed.text: The neighbours' little ones won't leave you alone: tell us a story, tell us a story. And suddenly you begin that same tale about the clever tortoise - with the ending you made up yourself as a child.
ev.k2_tale_passed.same: Tell it the way you remember
ev.k2_tale_passed.same.ok: At the part where the tortoise tricks the giant the second time, the little ones squealed with delight - exactly as you once did.
ev.k2_tale_passed.new_end.success: The new ending was even better than the old one. Now the little ones want only that one - every evening, word for word.
ev.k2_tale_passed.new_end.failure: The little ones didn't like the new ending. 'That's wrong!' they shouted, and demanded the old one.
ev.k2_first_chore.title: The first errand
ev.k2_first_chore.text: {npc}, your mother, has trusted you with a real task for the first time: to carry a little pot of hot food to a sick neighbour three houses away. 'Don't run and don't peek,' she said.
ev.k2_first_chore.careful: Carry it slowly, with both hands
ev.k2_first_chore.careful.success: You delivered every drop. The neighbour stroked your head and pressed something sweet into your hand, and that evening your mother told everyone who came by.
ev.k2_first_chore.careful.failure: On the very last step you tripped on the threshold. Half the food ended up on the ground, but the neighbour said half was more than enough for her.
ev.k2_first_chore.peek: Peek under the lid on the way
ev.k2_first_chore.peek.success: You peeked, sniffed and licked a finger. Nobody noticed, and the neighbour praised the cooking.
ev.k2_first_chore.peek.failure: The lid slipped out of your hand and rolled under people's feet. You chased it the length of the street while the pot went cold on the ground.
ev.k2_first_chore.run: Run, to get it done faster
ev.k2_first_chore.run.success: You got there faster than the wind, and the food was still hot. The neighbour laughed: 'What a messenger!'
ev.k2_first_chore.run.failure: You went sprawling in the middle of the street. The hot food burned your hand, and the little pot cracked in two.
ev.k2_tantrum.title: The storm
ev.k2_tantrum.text: {npc}, your father, wouldn't take you with him. You threw yourself on the ground in the middle of the yard, screaming and drumming your heels so hard that the neighbours came running.
ev.k2_tantrum.scream.success: Your father gave in and put you on his shoulders. You rode along, proud and tear-stained, hiccuping all the way.
ev.k2_tantrum.scream.failure: Your father left, and the neighbours chuckled about it for a long time. You screamed until you fell asleep right there on the ground.
ev.k2_tantrum.sulk.ok: You sulked until he came back. But he brought you a smooth pebble from the road, and it became impossible to go on sulking.
ev.k2_tantrum.follow.success: Your father only noticed you at the edge of the fields. He sighed and took your hand. It was the best day of the whole summer.
ev.k2_tantrum.follow.failure: After a hundred steps you lost sight of him and trudged back, sniffling. And at home you got into trouble as well.
ev.k2_share.title: Sharing
ev.k2_share.text: You are holding a ripe, sweet fruit - a whole one, all yours. Beside you stands a neighbour's little one, even younger than you, thin, in hand-me-downs far too big, looking not at you but at the fruit.
ev.k2_share.half.ok: You ate your halves in silence, at the same time, and then the little one suddenly took your hand and didn't let go until evening.
ev.k2_share.all.ok: The little one ate it all in a flash, stone and all, and looked at you in a way that made you not regret it one bit.
ev.k2_share.eat: Turn away and eat it yourself
ev.k2_share.eat.ok: The fruit was sweet, but somehow not as sweet as you had expected.
ev.k2_share_repaid.title: Half a fruit
ev.k2_share_repaid.text: At the market a stranger comes up to you and suddenly smiles: 'I remember you. When we were small, you gave me your fruit. I've never eaten anything sweeter since.' He has a stall here now - and seems to be doing well.
ev.k2_share_repaid.accept.ok: He filled a basket with his best goods and wouldn't take a thing for it. 'One good turn deserves another,' he said.
ev.k2_share_repaid.refuse.ok: You talked until the market closed. Since then he nods to you from afar, and the other stallholders respectfully ask how you two know each other.
ev.k2_dead_bird.title: The fledgling
ev.k2_dead_bird.text: Under the tree lies a baby bird fallen from its nest - bare, eyes shut. It isn't moving. You squat down beside it, and for the first time you don't know what to do.
ev.k2_dead_bird.warm.success: The chick suddenly twitched and cheeped. The grown-ups put it back in the nest, and every morning after that you ran to listen to it cheeping.
ev.k2_dead_bird.warm.failure: You warmed it until it got dark. The grown-ups said quietly that it would not wake up again, and for the first time you understood that this happens.
ev.k2_dead_bird.bury.christian: Bury it and put up a little cross of twigs
ev.k2_dead_bird.bury.islamic: Bury it and say a prayer over it, like the grown-ups do
ev.k2_dead_bird.bury.jewish: Bury it and put a pebble on top
ev.k2_dead_bird.bury.dharmic: Lay it on leaves and cover it with flowers, like the grown-ups do
ev.k2_dead_bird.bury.east_asian: Bury it and set a little cup of grain beside the grave
ev.k2_dead_bird.bury.polytheist: Bury it with a seed for the journey
ev.k2_dead_bird.bury.mesoamerican: Bury it with a kernel of maize for the road to the other world
ev.k2_dead_bird.bury.andean: Bury it with a kernel of maize so it won't go hungry
ev.k2_dead_bird.bury.african: Bury it and ask the ancestors to look after it
ev.k2_dead_bird.bury.ok: You dug a little hole with a stick and sat by the mound for a long time. The grown-ups left you alone.
ev.k2_dead_bird.ask: Ask the grown-ups why it isn't moving
ev.k2_dead_bird.ask.ok: They told you that everything alive falls asleep for good one day, and as for where it goes, everyone has their own thoughts. You thought about it all evening.
ev.k2_stuck_high.title: Up high
ev.k2_stuck_high.text: You climbed the tree by the fence - higher than you were allowed, higher than you meant to. Going up was easy. Looking down is frightening, and the branch under you is quietly creaking.
ev.k2_stuck_high.shout.ok: The whole household got you down, with plenty of noise and advice. For a long time afterwards they told the neighbours how you'd clung to that branch like a frightened little animal.
ev.k2_stuck_high.climb_down.success: Branch by branch, not looking down, you made it down on your own. At the bottom your knees shook so hard you had to sit on the ground for a while.
ev.k2_stuck_high.climb_down.failure: The last branch snapped. You landed in the dust with a thump, couldn't breathe for a long moment, and then howled more from hurt pride than from pain.
ev.k2_stuck_high.stay.ok: From up there you could see everything: roofs, roads, far-off fields and people the size of ants. Nobody missed you until evening, and they had to get you down by firelight.
ev.k2_altar_food.title: Not for you
ev.k2_altar_food.text: Treats have been left at the household altar - sweet balls and ripe fruit. The grown-ups say they are not for people. But there's nobody around, and the smell is making your stomach ache.
ev.k2_altar_food.text.polytheist: Treats have been left at the household altar for the gods of the house - a honey cake and ripe fruit. The grown-ups say you mustn't touch. But there's nobody around, and the smell is making your stomach ache.
ev.k2_altar_food.text.dharmic: On the little shelf before the image of the god lie sweet balls and a ripe fruit - an offering. The grown-ups say it's for the god. But the god doesn't seem hungry, and you very much are.
ev.k2_altar_food.text.east_asian: Before the ancestors' memorial tablets stand cups of fruit and sweets. The grown-ups say the ancestors eat first. But the ancestors are taking their time, and you are hungry.
ev.k2_altar_food.text.mesoamerican: Tamales and a bowl of cacao have been left before the clay figure of the god. The grown-ups say they are not for people. But there's nobody around, and the smell is making your stomach ache.
ev.k2_altar_food.text.andean: In the niche by the hearth, boiled maize and dried meat have been left for the ancestors. The grown-ups say they are not for the living. But there's nobody around, and the smell is making your stomach ache.
ev.k2_altar_food.text.african: A bowl of porridge and some nuts have been left at the little altar of the ancestors. The grown-ups say they are for the ancestors. The ancestors are silent; your stomach is not.
ev.k2_altar_food.eat.success: Nothing happened. No thunder, no lightning - just sweetness. You decided that whoever it was left for isn't greedy.
ev.k2_altar_food.eat.failure: You were caught with your mouth full. The grown-ups turned pale and spent a long time begging the altar's forgiveness - on your behalf. You felt ashamed and a little afraid.
ev.k2_altar_food.ask.ok: They explained that they eat first, and later the food will be shared among everyone. You waited until evening - and your wait was rewarded.
ev.k2_altar_food.leave.ok: You turned away and even screwed your eyes shut. That evening you were the first to be given a piece - the grown-ups had seen everything.
ev.k2_open_pen.title: Freedom for all
ev.k2_open_pen.text: You felt sorry for the animals shut up in the pen, so you opened the gate to let them go for a walk. They went for a walk - through the neighbours' vegetable patches, down the street and across somebody's washing laid out to dry.
ev.k2_open_pen.chase.success: You ran after every last one until dark, covered in dust and feathers, and got them all back in. The grown-ups just shook their heads.
ev.k2_open_pen.chase.failure: You chased them, they ran from you, and together you knocked over everything that was still standing. The neighbours all came to complain at once.
ev.k2_open_pen.hide: Hide and act as if it wasn't you
ev.k2_open_pen.hide.ok: They found you quickly: of all the children on the street, only you had a feather in your hair.
ev.k2_open_pen.blame: Say the gate opened by itself
ev.k2_open_pen.blame.success: The grown-ups grumbled about the wind and fixed the latch. You watched with the most innocent face in the world.
ev.k2_open_pen.blame.failure: Your footprints were right there by the gate - little ones, impossible to mistake for anyone else's.
ev.k2_m_shadow.text: All morning you tried to run away from your own shadow, and then to stand on its head. The shadow turned out to be cleverer.
ev.k2_m_echo.text: You shouted your name into a big empty jar, and the jar boomed it back. The two of you talked like that for half a day, until the grown-ups ran out of patience.
ev.k2_m_mud_cakes.text: You made a whole feast out of mud and solemnly served it to every grown-up. Each of them dutifully pretended to chew and praised the cooking.
ev.k2_m_ants.text: You spent half the day lying on your stomach by an ant trail, watching ants haul a crumb three times their size. You cheered them on as if they were family.
ev.k2_m_rhyme.text: You learned a counting rhyme and recited it to everyone - the neighbours, the dog, the pots on the shelf. By evening the whole street knew it, whether it wanted to or not.
ev.k2_m_why.text: 'Why doesn't the sky fall down? Why is water wet? Why don't you know?' By evening the grown-ups had started hiding from you in corners.
ev.k2_m_inside_out.text: For the first time you dressed yourself - back to front and inside out, but with no help from anyone. You were so proud that nobody dared change you.
ev.k2_m_asleep_bowl.text: You fell asleep at the meal, a piece of food in your hand and your cheek in the bowl. They carried you off to bed, but nobody managed to get the food out of your fist.
ev.k2_m_hiccups.text: Your hiccups wouldn't stop, so one of the grown-ups suddenly bellowed in your ear. The hiccups went away, but you were offended until evening.
ev.k2_m_frog.text: You brought a little frog home inside your shirt so it could live with the family too. It leapt out in the middle of supper, and the shrieks were heard down the whole street.
ev.k2_m_pot_drum.text: You found an old pot, turned it upside down and beat it with a stick all morning. You thought it was music. The neighbours thought otherwise.
ev.k2_m_moon.text: Someone showed you the moon, and you demanded to have it. They promised to get it for you when you're bigger, and you're still waiting, just a little.
ev.k2_m_bad_word.text: You brought home a new word from the street and said it loudly in front of guests. There was a long silence, and then someone choked on a laugh.
ev.k2_m_wasp.text: You wanted to stroke a stripy fly, and it stung you. Your finger swelled up like a pea pod, and you learned for ever that not everything stripy is friendly.
ev.k2_m_hand_shadows.text: One evening by the fire a grown-up folded their fingers, and a hare came to life on the wall, then a bird, then a horned beast. You tried to catch them with your hands until you fell asleep.
ev.k2_m_grass_whistle.text: A neighbour's boy showed you how to whistle with a blade of grass pressed between your thumbs. You blew until you were red in the face, and by evening the grass finally squeaked.
ev.k2_m_snail.text: You found a snail, gave it a name and carried it around in your palm all day. By morning it had crawled away - off on its own snail business, no doubt.
ev.k2_m_wet_mat.text: In the night you dreamed of a river, and in the morning your bedding was drying in the sun. Everyone in the house carefully pretended nothing had happened.
ev.k2_m_run_away.text: You took offence and left home for ever - as far as the corner of the next yard. For ever ended when you smelled supper.
ev.k2_m_reflection.text: For the first time you got a good look at your face in a bowl of water, and spent ages pulling faces at the strange child there. The child pulled faces back, which was very suspicious.
